risks.risk: Geopolitical and macroeconomic volatility (West Asia conflict, global growth slowdown)
risks.note: The forward-looking cautionary statement flags changes in government regulations/tax regimes, economic developments, exchange/interest rate fluctuations, competition and demand-supply constraints as factors that could cause actual results to differ materially. Business was directly hit in Q1 by 'Operation Sindoor', especially in the Chandigarh market, and the West Asia crisis raised raw-material/transport costs; near-term risk remains from continued geopolitical disruption to select international and corporate travel corridors and elevated fuel, logistics and utility costs.

risks.risk: Rising competition and new hotel supply
risks.note: Company explicitly identifies the risk from growing competition and new supply, which it counters by improving service standards and progressively renovating properties across its multi-brand portfolio.
Flagged as a risk the Company actively manages by constantly reviewing and implementing security measures at all its properties, reflecting the inherent exposure of high-profile hospitality assets.

risks.risk: Distribution/channel risk from online travel agents (OTAs)
risks.note: Increasing use of online transactions is raising the proportion of revenue shared with OTAs; the Company has taken measures to educate customers on booking directly via the Taj website and revamped the website to protect direct-channel economics.

Standalone operations are concentrated in just 5 hotels across 3 locations (Hyderabad/Telangana, Chennai/Tamil Nadu, Chandigarh), leaving revenue exposed to local demand or event-driven shocks in a small number of markets — illustrated by the Chandigarh market being specifically impacted during Q1 FY26.

risks.risk: Input and labour cost inflation pressure on margins
risks.note: Food and Beverages Consumed rose 8% versus F&B income growth of 5%, on higher raw-material and transportation costs linked to the West Asia crisis; Employee Benefit Expenses and Payment to Contractors rose 12% on merit increases, increments and negotiated union wage settlements, indicating persistent cost-side pressure independent of revenue growth.

themes.title: Hospitality & travel up-cycle
themes.need: Q1FY27 split hotels from airlines. INDHOTEL delivered a 17th consecutive record quarter - consolidated revenue INR 2,419cr (+15%), EBITDA INR 753cr at 31.1%, standalone occupancy jumping to 82% from 76% on a 41.8% standalone EBITDA margin, and asset-light management-fee income INR 168cr (+26%) - with management now framing the West-Asia war as a NET tailwind because outbound travel stays home; leisure RevPAR (Rajasthan/Goa) ran up high-20s. Airlines got the mirror image: INDIGO's EBITDAR margin collapsed from 28.0% to 15.6% on blended ATF of ~INR 140-150/litre versus INR 85-90 pre-war (fuel CASK +~80% YoY), leaving yield as the only defence. MHRIL shows domestic leisure premiumisation is real - Keystone average unit realisation +73% to INR 14.4 lakh on stable gross sales. LEMONTREE/CHALET/SAMHI/THELEELA ride the same occupancy-led room cycle; TRAVELFOOD/TBOTEK/DREAMFOLKS remain levered to airport PAX and B2B travel.
themes.driver: Occupancy-led (not rate-led) RevPAR compounding plus INDHOTEL's Ginger conversion cadence stepping 15->20->25->40 per quarter through FY27; for airlines the swing is INDIGO's guided Q2 PRASK growth of 'more than 25%' on flattish capacity against ATF cracks.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Sustained demand across leisure, business and social travel segments driving industry and company growth
- Structural demand-supply imbalance in Indian hospitality: ICRA projects demand growth of 8-10% CAGR versus supply growth of 5-6% during FY2025-FY2028, supporting occupancy and ADR
- Supply additions expected to remain measured due to higher land and construction costs, longer approval timelines and talent availability
- GST rate on hotel rooms priced up to Rs.7,500/day reduced to 5% (without input tax credit) effective 22 September 2025, improving affordability and supporting demand in mid-scale/budget segments
- Rising discretionary spending, an expanding middle class and continued business travel expected to support medium-to-long-term industry growth
- India's rising prominence in the global economy expected to attract higher inflows of foreign visitors, including heads of state and senior business executives
- Near-term risk: geopolitical developments in West Asia and related aviation disruptions could temporarily impact select international and corporate travel corridors while keeping fuel, logistics and utility costs elevated
- Industry outlook: hospitality sector expected to remain stable in FY2026-27, supported by domestic leisure travel and MICE demand, with room rates likely to remain firm; ICRA projects industry revenue growth of ~7-9% YoY in FY2026-27 with occupancy and ARR continuing to improve
- Company's strong domestic presence, balanced portfolio of owned/leased/managed properties, diversified brand architecture and stable fee-based income cited as platform for sustained growth and resilience

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Leverage IHCL as hotel operator (post new Hotel Management Agreements signed after IHCL's exit from the JV) to enhance guest experiences, strengthen market positioning and deliver sustained business growth
- Continued renovation/refurbishment of properties (rooms, public areas, F&B outlets) to maintain best-in-class guest experience and competitive positioning
- Leverage IHCL's broader operator ecosystem — advanced digital platforms, integrated business systems and data-driven insights — to improve operational efficiency and guest experience
- Sustainability integral to business philosophy: adopted IHCL's Paathya framework, advancing environmental stewardship, responsible operations and community engagement
- Grow via balanced portfolio of owned, leased and managed properties with diversified brand architecture across geographies/segments and a stable stream of fee-based income
- Board recommended a dividend of 100% (Rs.2 per fully paid-up equity share of Rs.2 each) for FY2025-26, consistent with the 100% payout declared for FY2024-25, subject to shareholder approval at the AGM.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Iconic, strategically located properties with premium amenities positioned for business, leisure and MICE demand
- Balanced portfolio of owned, leased and managed properties with diversified brand architecture and a stable stream of fee-based income
- Operated under the Taj brand via Hotel Management Agreements with IHCL, leveraging IHCL's operating platform, digital systems and service standards ("Tajness")
- Premier-wedding-destination and award-winning restaurant/bar positioning that draws local patrons beyond in-house guests

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Geopolitical and macroeconomic volatility (West Asia conflict, global growth slowdown) — The forward-looking cautionary statement flags changes in government regulations/tax regimes, economic developments, exchange/interest rate fluctuations, competition and demand-supply constraints as factors that could cause actual results to differ materially. Business was directly hit in Q1 by 'Operation Sindoor', especially in the Chandigarh market, and the West Asia crisis raised raw-material/transport costs; near-term risk remains from continued geopolitical disruption to select international and corporate travel corridors and elevated fuel, logistics and utility costs.
- Rising competition and new hotel supply — Company explicitly identifies the risk from growing competition and new supply, which it counters by improving service standards and progressively renovating properties across its multi-brand portfolio.
- Security/terrorism risk at hotel properties — Flagged as a risk the Company actively manages by constantly reviewing and implementing security measures at all its properties, reflecting the inherent exposure of high-profile hospitality assets.
- Distribution/channel risk from online travel agents (OTAs) — Increasing use of online transactions is raising the proportion of revenue shared with OTAs; the Company has taken measures to educate customers on booking directly via the Taj website and revamped the website to protect direct-channel economics.
- Geographic and asset concentration — Standalone operations are concentrated in just 5 hotels across 3 locations (Hyderabad/Telangana, Chennai/Tamil Nadu, Chandigarh), leaving revenue exposed to local demand or event-driven shocks in a small number of markets — illustrated by the Chandigarh market being specifically impacted during Q1 FY26.
- Input and labour cost inflation pressure on margins — Food and Beverages Consumed rose 8% versus F&B income growth of 5%, on higher raw-material and transportation costs linked to the West Asia crisis; Employee Benefit Expenses and Payment to Contractors rose 12% on merit increases, increments and negotiated union wage settlements, indicating persistent cost-side pressure independent of revenue growth.
